provenance.notes: AUTHORED FOR ONE EXPERIMENT. These are surface forms an English speaker uses for the activity, written by hand so the probe has a way to reach `obtain_medication` from query text at all. They are not evidence about the world, they are not a measurement, and nothing downstream may read them as either. Four of them — `pick up a prescription`, `prescription`, `fill a prescription`, `prescription refilled` — are the `activityPhrase` values the pre-registration itself states for its four target rows; the rest are further phrasings of the same activity, and they exist so the table is a statement about the activity rather than an index of the registered rows. The table declares SURFACE FORMS only: every `activity` here must be an `activity`-kind concept the compiled geographic model carries, and which entity kinds afford it, in which country, with what modality and on whose authority all come from that artifact. It is deliberately NOT a `@mailwoman/poi-taxonomy` synonym table: that package's phrases are venue nouns, each naming a single category, and an activity is afforded by a set of kinds — the distinction the boundary record's section 5.3 states.
